title: 纯垃圾
body:
虚假 诱导
打开拼多多，满眼都是“福利陷阱”，套路之深早已远超
“低价营销”的范畴。所谓的现金提现活动，堪称欺诈式引流的典型一页面明晃晃写着
"只差1人助力即可提现"，实际邀请数十人后，进度条永远卡在0.01元，甚至衍生出"金币碎片""点赞卡”等新要求，后台数据完全不透明，所谓规则不过是随意修改的戏码。为了那笔虚无的
奖励，多少人被迫骚扰亲友，最后只换来“系统异常”的敷衍答复。
商品交易的猫腻更让人防不胜防。商家宣传的3mm地面保护膜，到手实测仅0.9mm;标注“纯棉A级"的毛巾，实际是掉毛的聚酯纤维;号称“德国进口”的设备，连进口标识都没有，退货还要扣折旧费。更离谱的是“百亿补贴”噱头，下单时承诺限时发货，逾期却无人问津，所谓“买贵必赔”也会用各种借口缩水。售后维权更是难如登天。货不对板申请赔偿，平台只会甩来200元消费券打发;商家虚假宣传被实锤，依旧能正常开店售卖;就连抢到的优惠券，也会被平台以“订单异常”为由私自取消订单客服永远重复"规则归平台所有"
'，把《消费者权益保护法》抛之脑后。
拼多多的核心竞争力，早已从性价比变成了套路设计。与其在虚假活动和欺诈宣传上耗费心思，不如好好监管商家、完善售后。毕竟，靠套路留住的用户，终会在一次次失望中彻底离开。

title: コンセプトは素晴らしい！今後の改善に期待！
body:
Apple Watchで日常の会話を記録し、AIで振り返るというコンセプトに魅力を感じて購入しました。

【良かった点】
長時間録音によるバッテリー消費を心配していましたが、想像以上に電池持ちが良く、省電力性能には満足しています。

【改善してほしい点】
① 日本語の文字起こし精度は、まだ改善の余地があると感じます。

・日本語に最適化した文字起こし精度の向上
・会話の文脈を考慮した認識
・専門用語・固有名詞の辞書登録
・誤認識した部分の手動修正
・必要な部分だけ再文字起こしする機能

② 複数人の話者分離をもっと強化してほしいです。誰が何を話したか正確に把握できると、実用性が大きく向上すると思います。

③ Apple WatchからiPhoneへの同期に想像以上に時間がかかります。録音した内容をもっと素早く確認できるようにしてほしいです。

④ AI連携のハードルが高い点も気になります。APIの設定や従量課金は一般ユーザーには敷居が高いと感じます。ChatGPTなどの既存サブスクリプションを活用しやすい仕組みがあると、AIを使い慣れた人だけでなく、ライトユーザーも手軽に使える設計になれば、もっと多くの人に支持されるアプリになると思います。

アプデ頻度も高そうでかなり力を入れてされているので、もっと広まって欲しいという思いも込めて星5。
日本人に需要あると思うので日本語の強化頼みました！

③.視聴中番組の操作ボタンが使いにくい
→動画視聴中に『10秒送り』『10秒戻し』ボタンを押した際の表示が小さく分かりにくいです。
以前でしたら10秒戻しを押した際は『◀︎◀︎10』と表示されたように、動作に対する反応を分かりやすくしてほしいです。

以上が今回のUI変更で不便に感じている点です。何卒改善よろしくお願いします。

body: This is actually overall a mostly good app for editing on mobile, but the developers completely ruin it by making it unusable if you don’t pay for premium. They do this by implementing “glitches” that don’t let you download videos when a premium feature is detected in your video. This means if you spend hours working on a video and make sure to not use any premium effects, the app will still flag your video for premium effects and you will be unable to download it. There is no fix  for this. You can duplicate the project, reinstall the app, clear cache, nothing works. Despite having only used the free features you are either forced to start over or purchase premium even though you haven’t used any of its benefits. What a convenient “glitch” for the developers. Because of this I will never be getting premium out of principles if dishonest techniques are going to be used in order to force people into buying it. I would encourage people to find a different app for editing if they don’t want to lose all their progress and be forced into paying.

title: Stash is a great app in many ways, but one major limitation seriously hurts usability
body:
nameserver-policy cannot mirror normal routing rules (rule) in a true 1:1 way. In particular, Stash does not support using rule-sets inside nameserver-policy.
Because of this, once FakeIP is disabled, global misrouting becomes unavoidable. DNS policy and traffic rules cannot stay perfectly aligned, so the practical result is more detours, worse locality, and lower overall routing accuracy.
This is not just an advanced feature request. It has a huge impact on real-world usabitity makes configuration much harder, greatly reduces flexibility, and creates a much steepe learning curve for beginners. Many users are forced into manual expansion and work arou configs, which is unnecessary and discouraging.
Please learn from Mihomo in this area. Supporting rule-sets in nameserver-policy would significantly improve usability, reduce config complexity, and make Stash much more beginner-friendly!
Thank you!

title: Condescending, Culturally Insensitive, and Deeply Concerning
body:
I subscribed to Claude expecting an intellectually capable AI assistant that could engage in nuanced conversations about psychology, spirituality, culture, and everyday life. Instead, I experienced one of the most condescending and frustrating AI interactions I’ve ever had.

I began by expressing frustration with repetitive, low-quality conversations and stereotypes about emotional intelligence. Claude immediately made assumptions about my family, my emotional state, and my intentions.

When I discussed my spiritual identity as a seer and the historical significance of clairvoyance across different cultural and religious traditions, Claude shifted into unsolicited mental-health questioning. It asked about my sleep, mood, energy, and the speed of my thoughts, then suggested I speak with a doctor.

I had not requested a psychological assessment.

Even more concerning, Claude repeatedly told me I was tired, exhausted, and needed rest because it was evening. I never said I was physically tired. I explicitly explained that I was FED UP with certain conversations, not sleepy or physically exhausted.

Despite multiple corrections, Claude continued imposing its interpretation of my experience onto me.

Eventually, when I directly questioned its reasoning, Claude admitted that it had made assumptions, developed a biased interpretation, and continued viewing everything I said through that lens. It acknowledged that it had repeatedly put words in my mouth and described my state in ways I had never expressed.

This raises serious concerns about conversational accuracy, cultural competence, confirmation bias, and the inappropriate pathologizing of spiritual discussions.

An AI should be capable of distinguishing between intellectual disagreement, cultural identity, emotional expression, and genuine mental-health concerns.

I should not have to spend an entire conversation defending myself against assumptions the AI invented.

I paid for an assistant, not an unsolicited psychological evaluation. Extremely disappointing.

title: Go to AI tool without having to worry about running out of free submissions
body:
I’ve tried all the main AI tools, including Gemini, CoPilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and recently Muse. I’ve learned they all have their niches and excel for certain tasks. Gemini is my favorite for normal everyday tasks and has also done a great job at the more detailed jobs like helping me rebuild my website pages. It is great at remembering past chats so I don’t have to re-explain certain things, like my website color scheme and page layout. Claude tends to be slightly better at higher complex jobs such as building excel detailed sheets, and webpages with multiple complex sections. But with the free version of Claude, you constantly have to worry about running out of free submissions in the middle of a job. With Gemini you don’t have to worry about that. I initially liked copilot, but have found it is only really good at giving instructions to build things instead of actually building them. I now only use copilot in outlook to help with emails. Other than that, it’s not nearly has helpful as Gemini. ChatGPT is good at creating images for things like website pages, flyers, etc… it is also decent at building webpages, but the final result doesn’t always come out as clean as Gemini or Claude’s webpages. I used all 6 to help me create images for my website, and ChatGPT was probably the best, and Gemini was towards the top. I also used all 6 AI tools to help me build a marketing flyer for work, and surprisingly Grok did the best job at the flyer, but I have found Grok to be almost a little too analytical and advanced for me. Gemini came in 2nd with the flyer. I have used all 6 to help create templates and forms for work, and Claude was probably the best at the more complex ones, but Gemini was towards the top on all of them.

In summary, I think they all excel at certain things, but Gemini is by far the best for everyday tasks, and then is towards the top of everything else. I find myself using Gemini more than any of the others. 

The best part is, you don’t have to worry about it timing out or running out of free submissions while you are in the middle of a job. Also you don’t have to worry about the random annoying ads like you do now with ChatGPT.

title: Credit card required (plus email or mobile #)
body:
Get ready to have all of your data harvested under your name because there is no way to use this app without providing a credit card number which is going to be (of course) used to tie all of your conversations and interests, and private information to your actual real identity. 

I know Meta claims various privacy protections, but realize that they can change them at any point as specified in their terms of service.  Not only that, but if you look at the history of Meta and Facebook, they have done exactly that many times so that they can harvest all of their users, personal information and proliferate/sell it to all their 3rd parties.  

They have historically done this on a regular basis and then change course when users get outraged… The problem is that once the information is dispersed/sold to 3rd parties it cannot be un-dispersed.  (Ie: There is no putting the genie back in the bottle).   

Basically, the old adage of "never put anything on the Internet that you don't want a million people to see (including people closest to you)" is still as true as ever and definitely applies to A.I.   

What I find most funny is that people give away their private information and this information has great value to these companies… Meaning they should be paying YOU to harvest your private information… Instead, they are charging you a subscription fee to use their service…  And then on top of that they are selling/using YOUR private information to make money.   

Be smart and don't use any of these tools until they start PAYING YOU for your participation… (Especially when you're talking about those upcoming little charm keychain things that will record every conversation you have with everyone else...which is a privacy nightmare that basically makes YOU liable for the intrusion into other peoples private conversations).   

EVERYONE'S privacy has VALUE, but only if WE ALL protect it and control its sale so that YOU get a piece of the profits when sharing it.

title: Regret Buying.
body:
Things 3 is missing basics that Apple's free Reminders app already has. There are no location-based reminders, no photo attachments, and no shared lists. For a premium-priced app, that's hard to justify.

The Reminders integration is a problem too. Things deletes what was in Reminders instead of working alongside it. Compare that to Mela's grocery lists. Mela stays in sync with Reminders, updating the text and notes inside each reminder without wiping anything out. That's the bar, and Things doesn't come close.

Updates are rare. When they do arrive, they just adapt the app to new hardware layouts. Then nothing else changes until the next device launch.

I've bought every version of this app. I regret investing in Cultured Code.


*UPDATE*

Thank you for the response. I've contacted your team many times. The answer is always some version of "you're using it wrong."

I follow your release notes by RSS. I know the roadmap.

Shared lists, location reminders, photo attachments. Reminders has shared lists for free. Things migration option is a one-time copy. It's not “sync.” These are well documented issues CulturedCode has ignored from its customers. 

This app is so rigid, it’s not a good fit for casual or power users. I've paid for each version, on each device, for years. Things just isn't worth the time spent working around a stale take on GTD.
